groups.name: Web & App Engineering
groups.summary: Sites and web applications, from structure and interface through to a live, maintained service.

cards.name: HTML
cards.summary: Semantic document structure for accessible, crawlable web interfaces.
cards.what: I write clear, semantic HTML so pages are readable, accessible, and straightforward to maintain — including multi-page sites and single-page application shells.

cards.name: CSS
cards.summary: Layout, typography and responsive styling without a heavy framework.
cards.what: I style interfaces with plain CSS: compact spacing, clear hierarchy, and layouts that hold up on phones, tablets and desktops without pulling in a UI kit.

cards.name: JavaScript
cards.summary: Browser and server JavaScript for interactive interfaces and tooling.
cards.what: I use JavaScript directly in the browser and on the server for forms, search, real-time updates and small applications — without a required frontend framework.

cards.name: Node.js
cards.summary: JavaScript on the server for web apps, APIs and local tooling.
cards.what: I build web services and command-line tools on Node.js, including zero-dependency apps that stay on the standard library where that is practical.

cards.name: Responsive UI and UX
cards.summary: Interfaces that stay usable across phone, tablet and desktop.
cards.what: I design and implement interfaces with compact controls, clear focus states and layouts that work at small sizes first, then scale up cleanly.

cards.name: Zero-dependency web apps
cards.summary: Self-contained applications that do not require a heavy package tree.
cards.what: I ship self-hosted web apps that run with little or no third-party runtime, so the stack stays understandable, portable and under your control.

cards.name: Single-page and multi-site architecture
cards.summary: Information architecture for one site, or a set of sites that share patterns.
cards.what: I plan page structure, routing and shared chrome for a single application or a group of related sites, so navigation and content stay consistent as the work grows.

cards.name: WordPress
cards.summary: Self-hosted WordPress sites, themes, and plugin work.
cards.what: I set up and look after self-hosted WordPress sites: clear structure, themes and plugins, and the routine work that keeps a site running.

cards.name: Visual Studio
cards.summary: Building and debugging software with Visual Studio.
cards.what: I use Visual Studio to write, build and debug software, including Windows-focused work, with a clear project structure and a maintainable toolchain.

cards.name: GitHub
cards.summary: Public source control, issues and releases on GitHub.
cards.what: I use GitHub for public source control, issues and releases. Private repositories are not listed or linked on this site.

groups.name: Backend & Data
groups.summary: Services, storage, sign-in and the everyday data work that keeps a product running.

cards.name: Node.js standard library
cards.summary: HTTP, file and process work using the Node.js standard library.
cards.what: Where it is practical, I keep server code on the Node.js standard library — HTTP services, file I/O and processes — so deployments stay small and easy to reason about.

cards.name: SQLite
cards.summary: Embedded SQL storage for applications that should stay self-hosted.
cards.what: I use SQLite for application data when a self-hosted, file-based database is the right fit: simple backups, clear schema, and no separate database server to operate.

cards.name: Authentication
cards.summary: Sign-in, accounts and credential handling for web applications.
cards.what: I implement sign-in and account flows with careful handling of credentials, recovery and access control, suited to the scale of the application.

cards.name: Session security
cards.summary: Session cookies, expiry and protection against common session attacks.
cards.what: I set up session handling with secure cookies, sensible expiry and defences against session fixation and cross-site request issues.

cards.name: Automated backups
cards.summary: Scheduled copies of application data and configuration.
cards.what: I put automated backups in place for databases, files and configuration, with retention that can actually be restored from.

cards.name: CSV and PDF generation
cards.summary: Export of reports and records as CSV or PDF files.
cards.what: I generate CSV and PDF output from application data for records, invoices and operational reports, without a bulky reporting suite.

cards.name: Ollama
cards.summary: Running and managing local AI models.
cards.what: I run and manage local AI models with Ollama: installing models, keeping them up to date, and wiring them into local tooling when a self-hosted setup is the right fit.

groups.name: Infrastructure & Self-Hosting
groups.summary: Servers, DNS, certificates, mail and the operations work that keeps systems online.

cards.name: Linux servers
cards.summary: Provisioning, hardening and day-to-day operation of Linux hosts.
cards.what: I set up and operate Linux servers for web applications and services: users, firewalls, process management, and the routine work that keeps a host healthy.

cards.name: Debian
cards.summary: Debian servers: install, hardening and day-to-day operations.
cards.what: I install, harden and operate Debian servers for web applications and services, including updates, users and the routine work that keeps a host healthy.

cards.name: Docker
cards.summary: Container images, Compose files and local Docker workflows.
cards.what: I build and run container images and Compose files for local and server workflows, so services start the same way from one host to the next.

cards.name: Windows servers
cards.summary: Windows hosts for business applications, file services and local networks.
cards.what: I work with Windows servers in small business settings — applications, file services and the surrounding network — alongside Linux where both are in use.

cards.name: Windows desktop
cards.summary: Windows desktop setup, administration, troubleshooting and tooling.
cards.what: I set up and look after Windows desktop systems: installation, administration, troubleshooting and the everyday tooling that keeps workstations usable in a small business or workshop setting.

cards.name: Windows Automation
cards.summary: PowerShell scripting, scheduled tasks, and workstation automation.
cards.what: I write PowerShell scripts, scheduled tasks and workstation automation so routine Windows work runs on its own, with a clear, maintainable set of tasks rather than one-off manual steps.

cards.name: PowerShell
cards.summary: PowerShell scripting for Windows automation and administration.
cards.what: I write PowerShell scripts for Windows administration and automation: repeatable tasks, scheduled jobs and clear, maintainable scripts.

cards.name: DNS
cards.summary: Domain records, routing and mail-related DNS for live services.
cards.what: I plan and maintain DNS for websites and mail: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX and TXT records, including SPF, DKIM and DMARC, with changes made carefully.

cards.name: TLS and ACME
cards.summary: Certificates and HTTPS for public sites and services.
cards.what: I put HTTPS in place with automatically renewed certificates, and keep certificate and redirect behaviour correct as domains change.

cards.name: SMTP, DKIM and IMAP mail
cards.summary: Business email: self-hosted or managed, with correct DNS and authentication.
cards.what: I set up business email on a domain — self-hosted or managed — with SPF, DKIM and DMARC in place, and help with mailbox migrations.

cards.name: Reverse proxies
cards.summary: Front doors for web apps: TLS termination, routing and isolation.
cards.what: I place reverse proxies in front of applications for TLS, host routing and a single public entry point, so services stay isolated on the private side.

cards.name: Uptime monitoring
cards.summary: Checks and alerts when a site or service stops responding.
cards.what: I set up uptime and health checks so outages are noticed quickly, with alerts that go to the people who can act on them.

cards.name: Cloudflare
cards.summary: Workers, Pages and DNS as supporting infrastructure tools.
cards.what: I use Cloudflare Workers, Pages and DNS when they are the right supporting tools for a deployment — alongside self-hosted Linux and Windows infrastructure, not in place of core engineering.

cards.name: Cloudflare Proxying
cards.summary: DNS routing, proxying, TLS, and edge caching.
cards.what: I configure DNS routing, proxying, TLS and edge caching so sites are reachable and cached at the edge. This is supporting infrastructure work, not a headline skill.

cards.name: Azure
cards.summary: Microsoft Azure as a supporting cloud for compute, storage and networking.
cards.what: I work with Azure when a project already lives there or needs Microsoft cloud services, as a supporting platform next to self-hosted infrastructure.

cards.name: AWS
cards.summary: Amazon Web Services as a supporting cloud for compute, storage and networking.
cards.what: I work with AWS when a project requires it, using it as a supporting cloud platform rather than the centre of how I design software and systems.

groups.name: Protocols, Commerce & Crypto
groups.summary: Interfaces between systems, payments in everyday currencies, and on-chain settlement.

cards.name: RPC and JSON-RPC
cards.summary: Remote procedure interfaces, including JSON-RPC services and clients.
cards.what: I design and integrate RPC and JSON-RPC interfaces so applications can call remote procedures with clear, documented payloads.

cards.name: REST
cards.summary: HTTP APIs with predictable resources and error handling.
cards.what: I build and consume REST APIs with clear resource paths, status codes and JSON payloads, suited to web applications and integrations.

cards.name: WebSockets
cards.summary: Two-way connections for live updates in the browser or between services.
cards.what: I use WebSockets when a product needs live updates — dashboards, messaging or operational views — with reconnection and error handling thought through.

cards.name: MQTT
cards.summary: Lightweight publish and subscribe messaging for devices and services.
cards.what: I integrate MQTT for publish-and-subscribe messaging between services or devices, including topics, quality of service and retained messages where they are needed.

cards.name: Webhooks
cards.summary: Signed HTTP callbacks for events between systems.
cards.what: I implement webhook senders and receivers with signature checks, retries and idempotent handling so event-driven integrations stay reliable.

cards.name: Modular plugins
cards.summary: Extension points so features can be added without rewriting the core.
cards.what: I design modular plugin hooks so a product can gain features later without a rewrite of the core, with a clear contract for each extension.

cards.name: Multi-currency fiat checkout and subscriptions
cards.summary: Card and wallet checkout, including subscriptions, in everyday currencies.
cards.what: I implement checkout and subscription flows for payments in everyday currencies, including receipts and the operational pages a buyer needs after paying.

cards.name: Cryptocurrency wallets
cards.summary: Wallet flows for holding and sending supported digital assets.
cards.what: I build wallet-related application flows — send, receive and balance views — with careful handling of keys and confirmation, for products that need them.

cards.name: RPC nodes
cards.summary: Connections to blockchain RPC nodes for reads and transaction broadcast.
cards.what: I connect applications to blockchain RPC nodes for reads and transaction broadcast, with clear handling of node errors, fees and confirmation.

cards.name: On-chain settlement
cards.summary: Recording and confirming value transfer on a supported chain.
cards.what: I implement on-chain settlement in applications that need it: constructing transfers, waiting for confirmation, and recording the result against an order or account.
